_about: Pre-written answers for the Wellness Assistant. Each topic is picked by counting how many of its keywords appear in the question. To add a topic, add an entry here. No code change is needed.

topics.title: Sleep
answer: Most adults need at least 7 hours of sleep a night. A regular routine is one of the most helpful things you can build.
Try going to bed and waking up at about the same time every day, including weekends, and give yourself 30 to 60 minutes to wind down without screens.
tips: Avoid caffeine in the afternoon and evening.
Keep your bedroom dark, quiet and cool.
Get some daylight and movement during the day.
If you can't sleep, get up and do something calm until you feel sleepy.
topics.see_doctor: If poor sleep lasts for weeks, or you feel very tired during the day, speak to a doctor.

topics.title: Stress and mental wellness
answer: Some stress is a normal part of life, but long-term stress can affect your sleep, mood and health. Small, regular habits can help you feel more in control.
A simple breathing exercise can help in the moment: breathe in slowly for 4 seconds and out for 6 seconds, for a few minutes.
tips: Take short breaks, and spend time outdoors when you can.
Talk to someone you trust about how you feel.
Keep a regular routine for sleep, meals and activity.
Limit news and social media if they make you feel worse.
topics.see_doctor: If stress or low mood feels overwhelming or lasts more than two weeks, speak to a doctor or call Tele-MANAS on 14416 (free, 24/7).

topics.title: Physical activity
answer: The World Health Organization recommends that adults get 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity a week, such as brisk walking, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days.
You don't have to do it all at once. Short bursts add up, and any activity is better than none.
tips: Start with a 10-minute walk and build up gradually.
Choose activities you enjoy, so you keep doing them.
Break up long periods of sitting every 30 to 60 minutes.
Take the stairs or walk for short journeys when you can.
topics.see_doctor: If you have a health condition, or haven't been active for a long time, check with a doctor before starting something strenuous.

topics.title: Healthy eating
answer: A balanced diet gives your body the energy and nutrients it needs. A simple guide is to fill half your plate with vegetables and fruit, a quarter with whole grains and a quarter with protein.
Small, steady changes are easier to keep than strict diets.
tips: Choose whole grains such as brown rice, whole-wheat roti or oats.
Include protein such as dal, beans, eggs, fish, paneer or lean meat.
Cut down on added sugar, salt and highly processed foods.
Eat regular meals instead of skipping and overeating later.
topics.see_doctor: For advice on a medical condition, food allergies or losing or gaining weight, speak to a doctor or a registered dietitian.

topics.title: Hydration
answer: Your body needs water to control its temperature, digest food and stay alert. How much you need depends on your size, how active you are and the weather.
A simple sign that you're drinking enough is pale yellow urine. You need more when it's hot, when you exercise, or if you have a fever.
tips: Keep a water bottle with you through the day.
Drink regularly instead of waiting until you feel very thirsty.
Choose water over sugary drinks most of the time.
Fruit, soups and buttermilk also count towards your fluids.
topics.see_doctor: If you have a heart or kidney condition, ask a doctor how much fluid is right for you.
